docs.title: Authentication
docs.text: The system supports two authentication methods (configured in settings.py):

docs.title: CONFIG Mode
docs.text: Local user authentication with hardcoded credentials.

docs.title: OIDC Mode
docs.text:
LCSB SSO (Keycloak) authentication using OIDC.

Features: - Single Sign-On (SSO) - First-time users complete signup form - User information pulled from OIDC token

docs.title: Submission
docs.text:
• ref_name: Unique identifier (e.g., ELX_LU_SUB-1)
  • title: Submission title
  • current_status: Draft, Study Registration, Data Upload, or Completion
  • institution_accession: Institution identifier
  • created_on: Creation date
  • finalised_on: Date moved to Data Upload phase

docs.title: Study (SubmissionStudy)
docs.text:
• Study name, description, website
  • Ethics approval details
  • Study types/features (JSON)
  • Study contacts

This can refer to the originating experiment or cohort or publication.

docs.title: Dataset (SubmissionDataset)
docs.text:
• GDPR data types (JSON)
  • Scientific data types (JSON)
  • De-identification type
  • Legal basis for collection/sharing
  • Subject category
  • Consent status
  • Access restrictions
  • Samples information

docs.title: Attachment (SubmissionAttachment)
docs.text:
• Uploaded files (PDF, TXT, PNG)
  • Notes/descriptions
  • Files stay in the system (or they are stored in DAISY?)

docs.title: Landing zone

  • password

docs.title: Message (SubmissionMessage)
docs.text:

docs.title: Authorization Decorator
docs.text:
The system uses @app_authorization decorator for access control:

@app_authorization(
    allowed_roles=['admin', 'data_provider'],
    record_authorization={
        'entity': 'Submission',
        'entity_id_key': 'sub_id',
        'entity_ac_attribute': 'id'
    }
)

Logic: 1. Check if user is authenticated 2. Check if user has one of the allowed roles 3. If not admin + record_authorization specified: - Fetch the entity (e.g., Submission) - Check if user has SubmissionAccess for that entity - Deny access if no access record found

docs.title: Service Layer Functions
docs.text:
Key service functions in models/services.py:

  • create_sub(): Creates new submission with auto-generated ref_name
  • delete_sub(): Deletes submission (only if deletable)
  • steer_sub(): Moves submission to next state + sends notifications
  • revert_sub(): Moves submission to previous state
  • has_access(): Checks if user has access to submission
  • get_in_progress_submissions_shared_with_user(): Returns visible submissions for data provider
  • assign_role_to_user(): Assigns role to user
  • register_new_user(): Creates new user account

docs.title: Notification Types
docs.text:
Trigger Recipients Subject Purpose Draft → Study Registration Data Provider(s) "Submission [REF] initiated" Notify data provider to begin metadata entry Study Reg → Data Upload Data Stewards "Submission [REF] needs Upload Instructions" Request upload link creation Data Upload → Completion Data Stewards "Submission [REF] needs Verification" Request final verification New Message Added Relevant parties (Context-dependent) Facilitate communication

Notification Features: - All notifications stored in database (EmailNotification model) - Admins can view all sent notifications - Admins can manually resend notifications - Notifications sent asynchronously via threading s

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The Elixir-DCP system manages data submissions through a multi-stage workflow.

docs.title: Roles & Permissions
docs.text: two primary user roles:

docs.title: Global roles
docs.text:
• Admin: power user managing user and config
  • Data Steward: Create and manages submissions, and oversees the entire submission process
  • User: Can create submissions and become Submitter. Can be also added as recipient.

docs.title: Submission context roles
docs.text:
User roles assinged within the scope of the submission. - Submitter: Submitter is defined in the draft stage by user creating the submission.

If regular user creates a submission, it has to be Submitter. Otherwise, the submission cannot be steered further.

docs.title: State Transition Rules
docs.text:
1. Draft → MetadataSubmission
  2. ✅ Requires: At least one submitter and one recipient assigned, receiving project selected.
  3. ✅ Who can trigger: Submitter only

  4. 📧 Notification: Sent to submitter and recipient

  5. MetadataSubmission → Approval Data Upload

  6. ✅ Requires: Metadata should be complete (recommended, not enforced)
  7. ✅ Who can trigger: Submitter
  8. 📧 Notification: Sent to data stewards

  9. 📅 Records finalised_on date

  10. Approval -> Data Upload

    • Requires: Validation by DataSteward
    • Who can trigger: DataSteward
    • Notification: Sent to submitter
    • Records metadata_approved_on date

  11. Data Upload → Completion

  12. ✅ Requires: Data uploaded (verified externally)
  13. ✅ Who can trigger: DataSteward or Recipient

  14. 📧 Notification: Sent to data stewards

  15. Revert (Any State → Previous State)

  16. ✅ Who can trigger: DataSteward only
  17. ❌ Cannot revert from Draft (no previous state)

docs.title: Deletion Rules
docs.text:
• ✅ Can delete: Submissions in Draft state only
  • ❌ Cannot delete: Any submission that has progressed beyond Draft
  • ✅ Who can delete: Submitter or DataSteward

docs.title: File Upload Constraints
docs.text:
• Allowed file types: PDF, TXT, PNG
  • File size: Controlled by server configuration
  • Storage: Files stored in UPLOAD_FOLDER with UUID-based folder names

docs.title: Submission from a service clinicians / less involved parties
docs.text:
The provider is willing to upload the data but metadata submission is seen as annoying. Provider is either not researcher or has provided data in-kind.

Full metadata is not needed or not available - data not matching our data model - data for preliminary analyses

Although agreement was concluded, the provider has no real motivation to go through lengthy submission process.

E.g. partial data are uploaded by a clinician as part of a bigger data collection efforts.

LCSB is supporting the submitter as much as possible - legal agreement template - sometimes even running the upload commands from provider's environment

Should our researcher act as submitter? Or should he act as data steward?

  1. Researcher pre-creates the submission selecting project and themselves as recipient.
  2. Researcher pre-fills the submission and shares it with submitter.
  3. Submitter will log into the platform and confirms the metadata is OK.
  4. DS approves the submission
  5. Data is uploaded by researcher or submitter
  6. Recipient verifies the data and metadata is ok
  7. Recipient marks the submission as complete

docs.title: Legal support involvement (Linda) - metadata collection and a contract negotiation phase
docs.text: Contracts are being negotiated and an Annex should describe data being submitted to LCSB.

docs.title: A - metadata is collected before the contract is signed (default)
docs.text:
This is not always possible! Metadata collection can take time while legal framework covering other things has to be signed ASAP.

How many submitters do have access to one submission? Multiple people can edit and contribute (DPO, researcher, legal, domain expert, data manager,...) but these all should be from one institution only, no? WAYS OUT:

  • excel template for import (back to DISH :D)
  • multiple submissions

Can multiple submissions be linked to become part of one contract? - probably yes as long as the contract is signed by all submitting institutions

  1. DS/Owner selects a receiving project
  2. Submitter fills in metadata
  3. Submitter steers the status to Approval
  4. DS reviews the metadata
  5. Before the actual approval, DS/Linda can export the metadata and attach it to contract.
  6. Contract is signed and attached or put into DAISY and linked by DS from submission.
  7. Submission is approved.
  8. Submission is moved to Data Upload

docs.title: B - metadata is collected after the contract is signed
docs.text:
Metadata is not known or it takes quite some time to provide. Contract should use a simplified DISH/table to cover basic description of the data. It can be also used later to prefill the submission during initiation.

  1. DS selects a project AND contract covering the submission
  2. Submitter fills in metadata
  3. DS reviews the metadata and approves
  4. Data upload link is generated (the submission export could be uploaded to Contract entity in DAISY)

docs.title: Big data hosting projects - BIOMAP / Immniverse
docs.text: Data is to be provided before contract or after. The metadata must be detailed. Goal is to be able to build data catalog. 1. Postdoc creates submission 2. Select receiving project and contract, putting themselves as recipients 3. Metadata is provided 4. DS verifies the metadata is complete enough to allow secondary use 5. DS approves ...

docs.title: Internal submission
docs.text:
Data is already present at LCSB and it needs to be "formalized" and enriched by metadata, ingested, validated, ...

  1. Submission is created.
  2. Provider institution is LCSB, recipient is the owner, receiving project is project of origin.
  3. Contract - none? MTA?
  4. Metadata is prefilled. What about Study? Project of origin? Its the same as receiving project :/
  5. DS approves metadata ...

docs.title: ELIXIR hosting
docs.text:
Same as big data hosting projects.

  1. Submission is created by DS
  2. DS becomes recipient
  3. Receiving project is ELIXIR Hosting (child project???), HSA is selected
  4. Metadata is provided + attachements
  5. DS verifies the metadata is complete enough to allow secondary use

...

docs.title: Complete submission process
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    actor DS as DataSteward
    actor Submitter
    participant System as Elixir-DCP
    participant Daisy
    participant Email as Email Service
    participant LFT

    DS->>System: 1. Create Submission
    System->>System: Generate Ref ID (ELX_LU_SUB-X)
    System->>System: Set state = Draft

    DS->>System: 2. Configure Submission
    DS->>System: Add short description
    DS->> System: Select provider's institution
    DS->> System: Select recieving project
    DS->> System: Select covering contract [optional]

    System->> Daisy: Get institution list
    Daisy-->System: List of institutions (ROR etc.)
    DS->>System: Assign Submitter user
    DS->>System: Add submission contacts

    DS->>System: 3. Steer to Registration
    Note over System,Email: The Submitter account does not exist yet.
    System->>Email: Send notification to Submitter
    Email->>Submitter: Email: "Submission initiated"

    Submitter->>System: 4. Complete Registration
    Submitter->>System: Fill metadata for all entities (study, data, attachements) 
    Submitter->>System: 5. Steer to Data Upload
    System->>System: Validate all mandatory fielSubmitter were provided.
    DS ->>System: Validate metadata (contract must be provided)
    System->>System: Record finalised_on date

    System->>Email: Send notification to Data StewarSubmitter
    Email->>DS: Email: "DS upload instructions"
    System->>LFT: Generate upload zone
    LFT->>System: Upload link/information
    System->>Submitter: Upload link/information

    Submitter->>LFT: Upload data
    Submitter->>System: 7. Data upload complete
    Submitter->>System: Add Messages (status updates)

    Submitter->>System: 8. Steer to Completion
    System->>Email: Send notification to DS
    Email->>DS: Email: "Submitter verification"
    Note over DS,System: some kind of validation from ingestion module
    DS->>System: 9. Verify Submission
    Note over DS: Data ingestion and validation

    DS->>System: Review all data and metadata
    System->>System: Mark as completed

    Note over DS,System: Submission Process Complete
